LAgeDOr: L'Age d'Or ( French : L'Âge d'Or , pronounced: [lɑʒ dɔʁ] ), commonly translated as The Golden Age or Age of Gold , is a 1930 French surrealist comedy directed by Luis Buñuel about the insanities of modern life, the hypocrisy of the sexual mores of bourgeois society and the value system of the Roman Catholic Church . rv: L' Age D' Or is hardly a comedy. It is a serious attempt to make a serious surrealist film. It does not have the bite of the Andalusian Dog but it is some what sad that Bunuel hated the religion he was raised with. Dali quickly returned to the church. and was kicked out of the group. Bunuel had to go to Mexico once the war started and his mother had to cut back on his allowance. He had to lean how to function in the commercial film studios in Mexico but eventually had a chance to make some very interesting films- none of which were comedies.

rv: In this atypical Jem Handy movie, the glories of America are narrowed down to the glories of Automobile production. In this spinning of events, The 'making' of things is loosely explored, from the boys making sandcastles (too close to the water!) to Mother preparing dinner (ham and cheese sandwiches!), this is a thinly veiled exploration until the film focuses on the REAL makers! The assembly line! From the historical re-enactments, with dialogue (if my memory serves me correctly, this is one of few rare times these films had actors saying anything rather then the narrator saying it for them)

No, no, no, no. This is not a film with sandcastle building kids. It is not "American Maker." It is not a Jam Handy film. It has nothing to do with Chevrolets. How can anyone post an incorrect "shot list" or review? Don't they actually watch the film first? Anyway, this is a 15-minute exercise narrated by Chet Huntley, whose contract must have allowed him to do side work away from NBC. It's entitled "American Women, Partners in Research."
